price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: shot mix (rim / mid-range / three-point shares, shot distance zones)
lineup fixed effects and shooter selection
methodological_questions: Can a within-team, within-game lineup-change design detect shot-mix shifts as a positive control?
How can a mechanical composition effect (different players take different shots) be separated from a causal lineup effect?
How should confounding from opponent, game state, clock and fatigue be handled when comparing lineups?
Is there enough exposure per five-man unit, or must the contrast be at the single-player-swap level?
How should shot mix be defined reliably from play-by-play shot distance and action types?

historical_evidence.finding: PULL_UP exposure-effect diagnostics: the PULL_UP-specific decline with exposure was -0.0255 (SE 0.0061) with lineup FE and -0.0063 (SE 0.0036) without lineup FE. A same-shooter placebo on other play types was about -0.0075. The record attributes this to a shooter-level confound (limited by confounding; risks CONFOUNDING and PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE; verdict artifact_found).

Tail/null-model audit of a published suppression excess: the excess (0.4080) was reproduced, but a within-unit permutation null gave a residual of only +0.0054 (z 0.40). The record lists limits of drift, insufficient exposure and selection/regression to the mean, and risks DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MECHANICAL_FLOOR and PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.

Double-suppression stacking (POST_UP then PUTBACK) on the next star possession, with large baseline n but small stacked n (1,047). The record lists limits of implementation bug and small sample. It does not concern lineup-driven shot mix.

Penalty-state adaptation pilot (game x offense x period FE, with adjacent-state placebos): the penalty contrast was not distinct from the placebo contrasts, and SEs were not printed (sqrt warning). Failure mechanism recorded as E_unclear; risk PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Interpreting an exposure effect without separating it from the lineup/shooter composition
failed_approaches.why: The apparent effect changed size with lineup FE, and the placebo on other play types was similar. Recorded as C_artifact, limited by confounding.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating an excess over a matched control as evidence of an effect without a proper null model
failed_approaches.why: The within-unit permutation null reproduced almost all of the excess. Recorded as C_artifact, limited by drift, insufficient exposure and regression to the mean.

failed_approaches.what_failed: A pilot that relied on placebo contrasts for identification
failed_approaches.why: The target contrast was not distinct from the placebos and SEs were missing. Recorded as E_unclear, risk PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work on adjacent questions shows that lineup/shooter composition is a recorded confounder (FAM:SF-TMP-009, status artifact), so any lineup design must handle it explicitly.

Earlier project work shows that placebo and permutation nulls can erase an apparent effect (FAM:SF-TMP-009, FAM:SF-TMP-012, both artifact), and that placebo-only identification can be uninformative (FAM:SF-TMP-021, inconclusive).
Small stacked or sparse cells and implementation errors have limited earlier conclusions (FAM:SF09, inconclusive).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix, so the stated positive control has not been tested before in the retrieved records.
The retrieved records do not give any shot-mix effect size or variance, or the exposure of five-man units in the 2022-25 data.
They do not show that a composition-driven shot-mix shift would count as showing the design detects causal personnel effects.
own_inferences: A shot-mix shift after a lineup change is close to guaranteed by composition: players have different shot profiles. As posed, the claim is nearly tautological and a positive result is weak evidence about detecting causal effects.
A useful positive control should be defined as predicted detection: the shift should match the swapped players' own out-of-sample shot profiles, in direction and approximate magnitude.
A swap of one player (four shared teammates) has much more exposure than whole five-man units, so single-swap contrasts are the practical unit.
The earlier artifacts suggest including a within-unit permutation null and checks on both composition and drift, rather than relying on one placebo.
uncertainties: Number of distinct five-man units and possessions per unit and per single-player swap is unknown until counted.
Whether the shot-distance field is complete and consistent across the three seasons is unknown.
Whether substitution rotation intervals align exactly with play-by-play events is unknown, which risks lineup mislabelling.
Whether the retrieved records transfer to lineup shot-mix questions is uncertain; they concern other outcomes.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records do not answer the question. They changed the design from a simple lineup comparison to one with shooter/composition adjustment, a within-unit permutation null and a pre-specified rule, because earlier lineup-related work produced artifacts and placebo-dependent results. The decision moved from proceed to proceed_with_changes.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved family tests lineup change against shot mix. The retrieved records only supply methodological cautions about lineup confounding, placebo reliance, null models and sparse cells.

risks.text: Lineup changes coincide with score margin, opponent lineup, fatigue, foul trouble and clock. Within-team composition also differs by player role.
The effect is largely mechanical (composition). A positive result may follow from how lineups and shot mix are defined, so it cannot by itself show detection of causal personnel effects.
Many five-man units have few possessions. Analysis must use single-player swaps or pooled units with a minimum-possession threshold.
Shot-mix shares are noisy at small possession counts. A minimum detectable difference must be computed before the analysis.
Lineups are built from rotation intervals and substitution events, and shot zones from distance fields. Timing misalignment or missing distance can misclassify them.
Player shot profiles used for the prediction must be estimated out-of-sample, excluding the game or stint being predicted.
Coaches substitute in response to performance, so the stints that follow a change may show regression to the mean.
Earlier work shows placebo-based claims can be non-distinct or fragile. A permutation null must be used alongside a placebo.
Shot profiles and league shot mix drift across seasons and within a season.
Several shot-mix zones, teams and seasons create multiplicity. Primary outcomes must be fixed in advance.
Lineup reconstruction and possession assignment are error-prone and need unit tests and reconciliation against box-score minutes.

design.estimand: For a single-player swap (lineup A to lineup B differing by one player), the change in the offensive stint's shot mix (primary: rim-attempt share, three-point-attempt share, and mid-range share of FGA), compared with the change predicted from the incoming and outgoing players' out-of-sample shot profiles. The positive control passes if the observed shift is in the predicted direction and correlates with the prediction.
design.unit: Team-stint pairs (adjacent stints within the same team-game separated by a substitution that changes exactly one player), aggregated to the swap-type (outgoing player, incoming player, team-season) level for inference.
design.sample: All regular-season and playoff games in NBA 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. Include stints with at least about 8 FGA on each side of the swap, exclude garbage time (margin and clock rule fixed in advance) and the final 2 minutes of periods. Reconstruct lineups from rotation intervals and check them against play-by-play substitutions. Use 2022-23 and 2023-24 to estimate player shot profiles and 2024-25 for the confirmatory test, with a rolling out-of-sample version as a robustness check.
design.power: Before analysis, count the swaps and FGA per swap in the data. Compute the minimum detectable shift in rim share, assuming binomial noise and clustering by team-game. Pre-specify that, if the median swap has fewer than about 8 FGA per side, the analysis pools swaps by player-pair type and reports the minimum detectable effect. Report the conclusion as underpowered if the minimum detectable shift in rim share exceeds the smallest predicted shift of interest (for example 3 percentage points).
design.controls: Within team-game comparison, with fixed effects for team-game, period, score-margin bin, and opponent. Control for the outgoing player's profile and for time on court. The predicted shift is built from leave-game-out player profiles. Compare observed against predicted using a regression with a slope and calibration check.
design.falsification: (1) Within-unit permutation null: shuffle stint labels within team-game and recompute the effect, as in the earlier permutation audit. (2) Placebo swaps with a similar-profile player, which should give near-zero predicted and observed shift. (3) Time placebo: shift at a fake substitution time with no lineup change. (4) A check that the effect is not explained by composition alone: test whether the observed shift tracks the predicted one beyond a simple role label such as guard or big. The control is not passed if the permutation or placebo results match the main result.
design.multiplicity: Primary outcome: rim-attempt share. The other shot zones are secondary, with Holm correction across the three zones. Seasons and the rolling robustness check are reported without correction as a consistency check. No team-level subgroup tests unless pre-registered.
design.decision_rule: Supported if, in the confirmatory 2024-25 sample, the slope of observed on predicted rim-share shift is positive and its 95% CI excludes 0, and the permutation null p<0.01, and placebo swaps are not distinguishable from zero. Rejected if the slope CI is within a pre-specified small bound and the minimum detectable effect is below the smallest effect of interest. Uncertain/underpowered if the minimum detectable effect is above that effect. Artifact if the effect disappears under the permutation null or drift-centered check. A supported result is reported only as showing that the pipeline detects composition-driven shot-mix change, not a causal lineup effect beyond composition.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for the 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, as available on 2026-11-02; the play-type possession graph database is used only for secondary cross-checks. Freeze a data snapshot and a lineup-reconstruction code version with a hash before analysis.

methodological_questions: Can a within-team lineup-change design detect shot mix shifts as a positive control?
How to handle confounding from opponent, game state, and minutes context when comparing lineups?
What sample size and exposure sparsity issues arise for five-man units?
How to define shot mix (shot distance zones, action types) reliably from play-by-play?
args.query: Does changing the offensive five-man lineup shift shot mix, and does this serve as a positive control showing the design can detect personnel effects?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether to call any more tools, but the budget is fine and I can just finish now. The retrieved records don't speak to lineup-change shot mix directly, so I need to report each one's status as it was recorded rather than as I might read it.

The question here is whether changing the offensive five actually shifts shot mix, which would show the design can pick up personnel effects. That's close to guaranteed mechanically, since different players take different shots, so the real work is making the control test something beyond composition. I'm planning a within-team, within-game stint comparison across distance zones, predicting lineup shot mix from each player's pre-period profile out of sample, with a shuffled-lineup placebo and a minimum detectable effect on rim share around 3 points.

I'm checking the remaining sparsity concern: the five-man units produce many unique lineups, so I'll keep only stints with enough possessions and run single-player swap contrasts. I'm also sizing my expectations, putting most of the probability on a supported outcome, and settling on a proceed-with-changes decision, since the design now includes lineup and shooter fixed effects and a placebo rather than leaning on the placebo alone.

I'm weighing whether to call any more tools, but the budget is fine and I can just finish now. The retrieved records don't speak to lineup-change shot mix directly, so I need to report each one's status as it was recorded rather than as I might read it.

The question here is whether changing the offensive five actually shifts shot mix, which would show the design can pick up personnel effects. That's close to guaranteed mechanically, since different players take different shots, so the real work is making the control test something beyond composition. I'm planning a within-team, within-game stint comparison across distance zones, predicting lineup shot mix from each player's pre-period profile out of sample, with a shuffled-lineup placebo and a minimum detectable effect on rim share around 3 points.

I'm checking the remaining sparsity concern: the five-man units produce many unique lineups, so I'll keep only stints with enough possessions and run single-player swap contrasts. I'm also sizing my expectations, putting most of the probability on a supported outcome, and settling on a proceed-with-changes decision, since the design now includes lineup and shooter fixed effects and a placebo rather than leaning on the placebo alone.
